title: Science vs. Myths: Fact Flip
theme: Scientific Facts vs. Common Myths & Misconceptions
description: Replace myths and misconceptions with scientific facts! Every disc you place represents a verified scientific fact that flips common myths to evidence-based truths. Learn critical thinking, the scientific method, and evidence-based reasoning while battling misinformation.
learning_objectives: Develop critical thinking skills by distinguishing fact from fiction
Learn about the scientific method and how evidence supports conclusions
Understand common myths and why they persist in popular culture
Practice evidence-based reasoning through strategic gameplay
Build confidence in questioning unverified claims
how_to_play: Place a Scientific Fact disc on the board adjacent to a Common Myth disc.
Any myth discs caught in a straight line between your new fact and an existing one are flipped to scientific facts.
You must debunk at least one myth with each move — if you can't, your turn is skipped.
Corners are like foundational scientific laws — once established, they can never be overturned!
The game ends when no more moves can be made by either side.
The side with the most discs on the board wins — can science prevail over myths?

storybook_pages.title: The Myth Busters Lab
storybook_pages.text: Welcome to the Myth Busters Lab! Misconceptions are spreading across the board — flat Earth claims, anti-science rumors, and old wives' tales. As a young scientist, your mission is to replace every myth with a verified scientific fact. Grab your lab coat and let the fact-flipping begin!
storybook_pages.image_prompt: colorful science lab with a young scientist in a lab coat, magnifying glass revealing facts hidden behind myth clouds, beakers and test tubes on a game board, bright educational cartoon style

storybook_pages.title: Facts Beat Fiction
storybook_pages.text: A single well-placed fact can debunk multiple myths at once! Position your scientific evidence at corners and edges for maximum impact. But watch out — myths are stubborn and the opposition will try to spread misinformation back across the board.
storybook_pages.image_prompt: game board with green science icons flipping red myth icons, lightbulbs appearing over converted tiles, a microscope and telescope in the background, educational cartoon style with sparkle effects

storybook_pages.title: Science Wins!
storybook_pages.text: As the board fills with scientific facts, the fog of misinformation clears. Count your facts and see how much of the board you've illuminated with evidence-based truth. Every myth debunked makes the world a little smarter!
storybook_pages.image_prompt: completed game board glowing with green science tiles, a trophy shaped like a microscope, happy diverse kids celebrating, myth clouds dissipating, bright cheerful cartoon style

flip_narratives: Science prevails! You debunked {count} myth(s) with evidence!

ai_flip_narratives: Misinformation spreads! {count} of your facts were overshadowed by myths!

transfer_exercises.game_context: Converting opponent's pieces by outflanking them
transfer_exercises.real_world: Changing someone's opinion by addressing their perspective before making your argument
transfer_exercises.challenge: Practice the 'reversal' technique in a real disagreement: fully articulate the other person's view before sharing yours.

transfer_exercises.game_context: Adjusting strategy as the board flips dramatically
transfer_exercises.real_world: Re-evaluating your approach when new information changes the picture
transfer_exercises.challenge: Think of a belief you hold strongly. List three pieces of evidence that might make you reconsider it.

glossary_terms.definition: The process of selecting among alternatives based on available information and values.
glossary_terms.example: Choosing between two career paths based on income, passion, and long-term growth.
glossary_terms.deep_dive: Good decision-making combines rational analysis with awareness of cognitive biases that distort judgment.
glossary_terms.real_world_example: Leaders make high-stakes decisions daily — the quality of their process matters as much as the decision itself.

glossary_terms.definition: Analyzing information objectively to form a well-reasoned judgment.
glossary_terms.example: Questioning whether a statistic is representative before using it to make a decision.
glossary_terms.deep_dive: Critical thinking involves identifying assumptions, evaluating evidence, and considering alternative perspectives.
glossary_terms.real_world_example: Journalists fact-check before publishing; scientists replicate experiments before claiming discoveries.

glossary_terms.definition: The belief that abilities can be developed through effort and learning from failure.
glossary_terms.example: Seeing a poor game result as feedback on what to practice, not evidence of being bad at the game.
glossary_terms.deep_dive: Research by Carol Dweck shows people with growth mindsets achieve more and recover better from setbacks.
glossary_terms.real_world_example: Students who believe intelligence is fixed give up when challenged; those with growth mindset persist and improve.

achievements.name: Flip Master

cultural_context: Scientific literacy and critical thinking are NEP 2020 priorities, with India actively working to reduce pseudoscience and promote evidence-based reasoning. This game builds the analytical skills needed to distinguish verified science from popular myth.
reflection_prompt: Which flip changed the shape of the game most? What did you not see coming?
